precisionDefaults.text: torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 defaults to False (since PyTorch 1.12): fp32 matmuls on Ampere+ do not use TF32 unless enabled.
torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 defaults to True: cuDNN convolutions may use TF32 on Ampere+.
torch.set_float32_matmul_precision default is 'highest' (full fp32); 'high' allows TF32 or bf16x2 splitting, 'medium' allows bf16; the doc notes it currently affects CUDA only.

Newer fp32_precision knobs (torch.backends.fp32_precision, torch.backends.cuda.matmul.fp32_precision, torch.backends.cudnn.conv/rnn.fp32_precision) take 'ieee' or 'tf32'; 'bfx9' is CUDA-matmul only, needs a CUDA 12.9+ build and errors on ROCm.
On ROCm, TF32 is supported on Instinct MI300 (gfx942) via hipBLASLt through the same torch.backends.cuda.matmul controls, with hardware-level numerical differences from NVIDIA.
torch.autocast default dtype: torch.float16 for CUDA, torch.bfloat16 for CPU (from torch.get_autocast_dtype()).
XPU autocast has its own op lists ('XPU Ops that can autocast to float16'), marked experimental; gradient scaling notes float16 is the default on CUDA and XPU.

Built-in autocast devices (including 'mps') accept only torch.float16 or torch.bfloat16 as the autocast dtype; other dtypes disable autocast with a warning. The amp docs do not document MPS op lists or its default dtype.
MPS does not support torch.float64 (Metal Shading Language has no double type); creating or moving a float64 tensor to 'mps' raises TypeError and PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK=1 does not help.
XPU float64: Intel Arc A-Series graphics has no native FP64; GradScaler requires FP64 hardware support, so disable it on Arc A-Series. Data Center GPU Max has FP64.
bfloat16 autocast on CUDA requires torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported() (Ampere or newer); otherwise autocast raises and asks for float16.
